title: The specified forward graph comparison at a geometric base change
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $f:U\to X$ separated etale between arbitrary schemes, $c$ a compactification, and $y\in X$. Put $g:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}\to X$ for the geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], $h:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}\times_X U\to U$, and let $f_g,c_g$ be the pulled-back morphism and compactification. For the actual derived graph maps $a,a_g$ of [def-asd-compact-support-graph-comparison], the equality of unbounded derived natural transformations is $(Dg^*a);C_c=C_\Sigma;(a_gDh^*)$, where $C_c$ is exactCompactSupportExchange and $C_\Sigma$ is exactEtaleSumExchange. This is a forward-map equation and makes no isomorphism claim.

proof.text: Construct the clopen graph transfer on unbounded derived categories. The graph section of a compactification is an open and closed immersion. Restrict to it, use the pullback section isomorphism and the open-extension unit, then extend by zero using the two clopen adjunctions. The pullback composition coherence, the open-extension mate formula and the base-change cube identify its pullback with the transfer for the base-changed graph. Compose with the proper projection unit and inverse proper base change, then transpose under the etale sum-extension adjunction. The resulting comparison commutes with base change by the adjunction unit law.

proof.text: Identify this derived comparison with the specified compactSupportDerivedComparison of etaleCompactificationGraphMap. On sheaves, the graph projection is the unit of restriction followed by the section isomorphism. The graph-composition comparison is the unique left-adjoint comparison, so its transpose is the open-extension unit followed by the pullback composition isomorphism. Thus the sheaf transfer is the same clopen unit-map-counit composite. Apply this identity degreewise and pass to homotopy categories. Construct the clopen right adjunction by deriving the exact sheaf adjunction termwise and transporting restriction along its exact-functor comparison. Its counit is the inverse open-extension unit, by the termwise adjunction normalization and cancellation of the transport isomorphisms. Normalization of pullback composition, units, counits and proper base change identifies the derived graph transfer on Qh representatives with the termwise sheaf transfer. The sheaf graph-unit equation then identifies the two etale-adjunction transposes. Localization full faithfulness and injectivity of the adjunction bijection identify the natural transformations.

proof.text: Transport the base-change equation for the identified comparison along Lg* isomorphic to Dg* and Lh* isomorphic to Dh*. The etale sum-exchange is the inverse derived etale base-change comparison conjugated by those two isomorphisms. The compact-support exchange is its specified proper/open counterpart. Naturality cancels the transport isomorphisms. Specialize the arbitrary base-change morphism to the geometric point of y. This gives the original forward-map equality, with no added finiteness hypothesis on either scheme and no stalkwise detection of derived morphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem compactSupportGraphDerivedComparison_geometric_baseChange
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ X) [Etale f] [IsSeparated f]
    (c : Compactification f) (y : X) :
    Functor.whiskerRight
        (compactSupportDerivedComparison A f c (etaleCompactificationGraphMap A f c))
        (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (X.algClosurePoint y)).mapDerivedCategory ≫
      exactCompactSupportExchange A c (X.algClosurePoint y) =
    (exactEtaleSumExchange A f (X.algClosurePoint y)).hom ≫
      Functor.whiskerLeft
        (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)
          (pullback.snd (X.algClosurePoint y) f)).mapDerivedCategory
        (compactSupportDerivedComparison A (pullback.fst (X.algClosurePoint y) f)
          (c.ofIsPullback (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (X.algClosurePoint y) f).flip)
          (etaleCompactificationGraphMap A (pullback.fst (X.algClosurePoint y) f)
            (c.ofIsPullback (IsPullback.of_hasPullback (X.algClosurePoint y) f).flip)))
